key_insight: This paper shows that remote sensing multimodal large language models (RS-MLLMs) are powerful, but their performance depends heavily on whether they are used as domain-specific tools or general-purpose models. It highlights the current limits of cross-task generalization and where these models still need remote-sensing-specific adaptation.
problem_solved: It addresses the lack of a systematic understanding of how well existing MLLMs work for remote sensing image scene understanding, especially across different tasks and settings.
method: Surveyed the landscape of multimodal large language models for remote sensing image understanding.
Performed diagnostic evaluation to compare capability boundaries, generalization behavior, and task-specific weaknesses.
Analyzed whether remote sensing applications benefit more from domain-specific models or general-purpose multimodal models.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this paper provides a clearer guide for choosing, adapting, and evaluating MLLMs in remote sensing workflows. It helps identify when a general-purpose model is sufficient and when domain-specific tuning is likely necessary.
visual_elements: A side-by-side comparison diagram of domain-specific vs general-purpose RS-MLLMs
A task performance matrix showing strengths and weaknesses across remote sensing tasks
A pipeline graphic of remote sensing image understanding with natural-language interaction
An icon-based summary of evaluation categories such as classification, retrieval, and scene description
paper_title: Multimodal Large Language Models for Remote Sensing Image Understanding: Domain-Specific or General-Purpose?
paper_authors: Qiwei Ma, Chunping Qiu, Xinjun Cheng, Xiaoyu Zhang, Puhong Duan
